features_intro: Everything below is in 1.0, checked by tests, and documented.

features.name: Command blocks
features.text: With zsh, bash, fish or PowerShell, each finished command becomes a block with its exit code, duration, folder and colored output. Copy it, or run it again in one click.

features.name: Tabs and splits
features.text: Several shells in one window, split right or down, resized by dragging. Your layout comes back on the next launch: structure only, never output.

features.name: A real terminal
features.text: vim, htop, tmux, SSH and REPLs work as they do anywhere. Search the scrollback, click links safely, and a click can never start a program.

features.name: Plugins
features.text: Small WebAssembly files add palette commands, block labels and status items. A plugin has no way to reach your files, the network or other programs.

features.name: Snippets and tasks
features.text: Keep commands with {{values}}, and find the scripts of your project (package.json, Cargo, Makefile, justfile) in the palette. They are typed for you to read; TermZip never presses Enter.

features.name: SSH and WSL
features.text: A tab that opens already connected, with your own agent and ~/.ssh/config. TermZip stores no key, password or identity file.

features.name: Twelve themes
features.text: Dracula, Nord, Catppuccin, Gruvbox, Tokyo Night and more, recoloring the whole window. Import iTerm2, Windows Terminal, Ghostty, Kitty and Alacritty themes as they are.

features.name: Yours to shape
features.text: Rebind every shortcut, tie a profile to a folder, tune cursor, spacing and window blur. Git branch and state sit in the status bar and can be turned off.

features.name: Accessible
features.text: Optional screen reader support, no motion when your system asks for none, and every interface color held to WCAG AA contrast in every theme.

perf_note: Windows is slower on a large flood of output; see the performance guide for every number and limit.

faq.a: Yes. TermZip is open source under the MIT license, with no accounts and no paid tier.

faq.q: Which systems does it run on?
faq.a: macOS (Apple silicon and Intel), Windows and Linux. Releases include a dmg, an installer and an msi, an AppImage, a deb and an rpm.

faq.q: Does TermZip send my data anywhere?
faq.a: No. There is no telemetry and no account. It uses the network only when you press a button: loading the plugin catalog, installing a plugin or checking for an update.

faq.q: Is it a real terminal, or a different kind of shell?
faq.a: A real one. It runs your own shell in a real pseudo-terminal, so vim, tmux, SSH and your line editor work unchanged. Blocks are added on top, for zsh, bash, fish and PowerShell.

faq.q: Why does my system warn me when I open it?
faq.a: Releases are not yet signed with an Apple or Windows certificate. Check the SHA-256 checksums published with each release, or install with Homebrew or Scoop, which check them for you.

faq.q: Can plugins read my files or use the internet?
faq.a: No. A plugin is a WebAssembly file with no imports, so it has nothing to call out with. It can only see what it asked for, and you approve that first.
